articles.title: Welcome to Magnite Space
articles.description: What each part of the workspace is for, and a sensible order to try them in.
sections:
Magnite Space is a desktop workspace for running, adapting and combining open language models. Inference, training, document search and workflows run locally. The app talks to the internet only for Hub search, model downloads and update checks.

The desktop window starts and supervises a local service on your machine. When the status in the title bar reads Connected, that service is ready.

AreaWhat you do there
Model hubSearch Hugging Face, compare models, estimate memory and download.
LibraryManage downloaded and imported models, trained adapters and projects.
TrainingFine-tune a model on your own examples with LoRA, then review runs.
BlueprintsBuild saved workflows from typed steps: models, data, search and tools.
DocsThis reference: app guides and the ideas behind them.
ConversationsChat with a model, give tasks in Tool mode, run a Blueprint, and use your documents through Knowledge.
SettingsAppearance, chat behavior, runtime engine, storage, notifications and updates.
A first path through the app

1. Download a small model in Model hub and chat with it.
  2. Add a few documents to Knowledge and ask about them.
  3. Try Tool mode to let the model request actions you approve.
  4. Build a Blueprint that turns a repeated task into a saved workflow.
  5. Train an adapter when you have examples of the behavior you want.
Find a model→Use it→Combine it→Adapt it

Search Docs from the box at the top of this page; results jump straight to the matching section. Save articles you return to, and use the back and forward arrows like a browser. Each article ends with links to the next article and related reading.

ShortcutsOpen Settings → General → Keyboard shortcuts for the full list.

articles.title: Download and chat with your first model
articles.description: Find a model that fits your machine, download it and get a reply in Conversation.
sections:
Open Model hub and search for a model family, or browse the most downloaded models. Small instruction-tuned models (under about 2 billion parameters) load quickly and are a good first test.

Open a model to see its details. The memory estimate adds the weights and the context cache for the context length you choose and compares them with your device. Treat it as advice: other applications share the same memory.

GGUF or Transformers?GGUF files run with llama.cpp and are ideal for chat. Training and Blueprint Model nodes need a Transformers checkpoint (Safetensors weights with a tokenizer).

Choose Download repository. The app downloads the whole repository into the shared Hugging Face cache and shows progress at the bottom of Model hub. One download runs at a time; Cancel download removes its unfinished files.

When it finishes, the model appears in Library. If a download fails part-way, its leftover files are listed in Settings → Storage & privacy → Partial downloads.
Load it and send a message

Choose Load in Conversation, or open a conversation and pick the model in the toolbar, then choose Load model. The engine is chosen automatically from the model format; you can override it under Model settings.

Type a prompt and press Enter to send (Shift+Enter adds a line). Stop ends a reply early. The meter in the toolbar shows how much of the model's context the conversation uses.

Model hub→Download→Load model→Send

Adjust Temperature and Response tokens in Model settings to change how varied and how long replies are. When you finish, unload the model to free memory for training or another model.

Read Tokens, context and what the model actually sees to understand the context meter, or Conversations for everything the conversation view can do.

articles.title: Find, download and manage models
articles.description: Search and compare models in Model hub, then organize models, adapters and projects in Library.
sections:
Model hub searches Hugging Face. Use Filters to narrow results by task, publisher and format, or show only models already on this computer. Sort by downloads, likes, size or name, and use Load more to see further results.

Tick Compare on up to three models to see their parameters, context length, license and size side by side.

A model page lists its parameters, maximum context, license and downloads. The memory panel estimates what loading it needs for a chosen weight format and context length. Provenance shows the publisher, revision and whether access requires approval; check the publisher's model card for license terms.

For a downloaded model the page offers Load in Conversation and Delete from this computer. Back returns you to the same place in the results.

Library has three tabs:

  • Models: everything downloaded or imported. Filter by source, load a model, or delete it. Use Import model… to add a GGUF file from disk without copying it.
  • Adapters: LoRA weights from Training or imported archives. Activate, export or delete them.
  • Projects: folders that group conversations and files. Pin the ones you use most.

Deleting a Hub model removes its files from the shared Hugging Face cache, which other tools may also use. A model that is loaded or used by a running training job cannot be deleted. Adapters trained on a model stop working until the model is downloaded again; the confirmation tells you how many.

Settings → Storage & privacy shows how much space the cache and workspace use, and lists unfinished downloads you can delete.

articles.title: Conversations: Chat, Tool mode and Blueprint
articles.description: The three conversation modes, model settings, adapters and how conversations are kept.
sections:
ModeUse it to
ChatTest prompts against a local model or a model with an active adapter.
Tool modeGive the model a task. It can propose actions such as reading a file or running a command, which you approve. See Tool mode.
BlueprintRun a saved workflow with your inputs and follow each step. New run and Run history work like New task and Task history. See Blueprints.

The gear icon opens Model settings: the engine (Auto follows Settings → Runtime), Temperature for how varied replies are, and Response tokens for the longest reply. The active adapter is shown here; Manage adapters opens Library → Adapters.

Activating an adapter reloads inference with its base model. Compare its replies with the base model on the same prompts to see what training changed.
The database icon opens Knowledge. Turn on Use in this conversation to add matching passages from your documents to each prompt; the passages used appear with the reply. See Knowledge.

Conversations are saved on this computer and listed in the sidebar under Conversations, where you can search them. New conversation starts a fresh one. Move conversations into Library projects to keep related work together.

The context meter shows how full the model's context window is. When a long conversation approaches the limit, start a new one or let Settings → Chat compact older messages automatically.

Your dataConversations stay in your data directory. Export or delete them all from Settings → Storage & privacy.

articles.title: Tool mode and the Pi harness
articles.description: How a local model works through tasks with Pi, and how you stay in control of every action.
sections:
Tool mode connects the loaded local model to Pi, an agent harness that runs in its own process on your computer. Pi gives the model a task, a set of tools and a structured way to ask for them. The model plans, proposes an action, sees the result and continues until it can answer.

Your task→Model proposes an action→You approve→Result returns to the model

Nothing is executed on the model's word alone: every action waits for your decision.

Open a conversation, choose Tool mode and load a supported local model. Describe the task and send it. Follow up in the same conversation to build on earlier turns, or choose New task for a clean context. Task history reopens a recent turn.

Small models can misunderstand tool formats. If replies are malformed, try a larger instruction-tuned model.

Each proposed action appears inline with exactly what will happen: the file or address to open, the file or folder to read, or the program, its arguments and working directory for a command.

  • Approve once allows that one action for this run.
  • Deny rejects it and tells the model.

An approval request expires after 90 seconds. Repeating the same request needs a new decision.

Commands run as youAn approved command runs with your account's permissions and can change files or start programs. Read every argument and deny anything you did not intend.

A task can take at most six model turns and four actions. Commands get a direct argument list (no shell) and a 30-second time limit, and their output is returned to the model. The default working directory is tool-workspace inside the app's data folder.

The run record keeps inputs, outputs and a redacted log of decisions. Treat it as private data when you back up or share your profile.

articles.title: Knowledge: chat with your documents
articles.description: Add documents, tune how they are split and searched, and use them in conversations and Blueprints.
sections:
Open a conversation and choose the database icon to open Knowledge. Under Documents, choose Add files… to index PDF, text, Markdown or HTML files. Each document has a switch to include or leave it out. The first time, the embedding model is downloaded. Your original files are never changed or moved.

Scanned PDFs without a text layer cannot be read; extract the text first.

Each document is split into chunks of a set number of words, with some overlap so ideas that cross a boundary are kept together. Each chunk is turned into an embedding: a vector that places similar meanings close together.

Document→Chunks→Embeddings→Search index

Change chunk size, overlap and the embedding model under Retrieval settings at the bottom of the panel. Changing the embedding model offers to Re-index existing documents.
Search and use it in a conversation

Use Try a question to preview which passages match before you ask the model. Hybrid search combines keyword and vector matching. Choose which documents are included with Select sources.

Turn on Use in this conversation at the top of the panel. Matching passages are added to each prompt and shown with the reply, so you can check where an answer came from.

Retrieval is not memoryThe model reads the passages for this prompt only. A good match does not guarantee a faithful answer; compare the reply with the source passage.

The Knowledge node in Blueprints searches the same documents and returns numbered passages ready for a Model prompt. See the node reference and Retrieval, context and model knowledge for the ideas behind it.

Select documents and choose Remove, or Clear all, to delete their index only; your files stay where they are.

articles.title: Build workflows with Blueprints
articles.description: Turn a repeated task into a saved, typed workflow of model, data, search and tool steps.
sections:
A Blueprint is a graph of steps (nodes) connected by typed ports. Data flows from inputs, through transforms, models and searches, to outputs. Because every port has a type, the editor can check a workflow before it runs and the trace shows exactly what each step received and produced.

Input→Transform→Model→Output

Open Blueprints in the sidebar. Create new starts an empty workflow, and the Request triage example creates an editable draft to learn from.

  1. Choose Add node and pick a card, or reuse one from Saved nodes.
  2. Click an output dot, then a matching input dot, to connect them. An output can feed several inputs; each input has one source.
  3. Select a node and use Configure to set its operation, ports and settings. For Model and Reasoning nodes, choose a downloaded Transformers checkpoint.

Workflow nodes lists every node and its links; selecting a link reveals the node at the other end.

Check readiness reports missing bindings, incompatible adapters, token budgets and runtime needs. Save revision publishes the current graph; earlier revisions are kept.

Open Test & run to test one node with sample inputs or run the whole workflow. Inputs are a JSON object keyed by Input node, or plain text when there is a single text input. The run trace shows each step's inputs, outputs and timing. Run history reopens earlier runs, even after the graph changes.

Choose Open in Conversation, or pick Blueprint mode in a conversation and select a workflow. The picker shows each workflow's latest saved revision. Tool nodes ask for approval inline, just like Tool mode.

Runs you start here form a session. New run starts an empty one, and Run history reopens any earlier run, with its workflow selected so you can run it again. Runs are saved on this computer, so history survives a restart.

To specialize one Model step, open Training jobs… on a saved Model or Reasoning node and add examples with named inputs and outputs. When the job completes, select the new weights on an Adapter node connected to the model's LoRA adapter input.

One run at a timeUp to eight runs can wait in the queue; they execute one at a time and release the checkpoint when they finish.

articles.title: Blueprint node reference
articles.description: Every node you can add to a Blueprint, what it takes and what it returns.
sections:
NodeWhat it does
InputTakes a value supplied when the run starts and emits it.
DatasetProvides typed JSON rows, inline or from a dataset imported in Training.
KnowledgeSearches Knowledge documents for a query and returns results plus numbered context passages.
OutputExposes a typed value in the run result.

OperationResult
Pass throughForwards a value unchanged.
Parse JSONTurns JSON text into a typed value.
Get object field / Get first itemPicks one field from an object, or the first item of an array.
Count itemsReturns the length of an array.
Format as textTurns any value into text; structured values become JSON.
Provide a constantEmits a fixed value saved on the node.
Build an objectCombines named inputs into one object.
Fill a text templateInserts inputs into text with {key} placeholders.
Compare two valuesReturns true or false for equals, ordering or contains.
Choose a valueReturns one of two inputs based on a condition. Both inputs are computed.
Validate dataChecks a value against rules and fails the step at the first problem.
Filter rows / Sort rowsKeeps rows matching a rule such as amount >= 100, or orders rows by a field.

NodeWhat it does
ModelGenerates text or typed JSON from named inputs with a local Transformers checkpoint.
ReasoningLike Model, for checkpoints with explicit thinking support; returns a typed final answer.
AdapterAttaches trained LoRA weights to a compatible Model or Reasoning node.
ToolRequests an action, waits for your approval, then returns a receipt.

For a Model node with several outputs, ask for a JSON object keyed by the output names. Plain-text response mode uses a single text output.

Ports carry text, numbers, booleans, arrays or objects. An integer output can feed a number input. Refine array and object schemas in the inspector, including item types and required fields. The key is used in connections and JSON; the label is what the canvas shows.

articles.title: Training studio and Observatory
articles.description: Set up a LoRA run, follow it live in Studio and review or compare runs in Observatory.
sections: Studio: set up a run in Train

Open Training. Train sits at the top of Studio: it holds the settings for your next run. Below it you see the latest run's results and saved configuration, so you can set up the next iteration with the last one in view.

  1. Choose a base model (a Transformers checkpoint, not GGUF).
  2. Choose an imported dataset, or Import file…: JSONL, CSV or plain text.
  3. Choose Edit settings to adjust the method (LoRA or QLoRA), epochs, learning rate, batch size and sequence length. Advanced settings and Output options hold the rest.

+ New run opens the same settings in a larger dialog. Save a recipe as a preset to reuse it. The resource estimate shows whether the run should fit your device.

Start the run and follow its steps, loss and device usage live. The Event log records what happened, including warnings and errors; use Follow latest to stay at the newest entry. Stop run asks the trainer to stop at the next safe point.

Base model + dataset→Recipe→Run→Adapter

Observatory keeps a local record of every run. Charts show loss, learning rate, gradient norm and throughput over steps. Compare baseline overlays another run, and Export run saves its record. Use in Train copies a run's settings into Train so you can change one setting at a time.

Read Interpreting loss and runtime measurements before drawing conclusions from a chart.
A finished run produces an adapter in Library → Adapters. Activate it and compare its replies with the base model on prompts it did not train on. See Anatomy of a training run for the full workflow.

articles.title: Anatomy of a training run
articles.description: How data, a base model, optimization and evaluation fit together inside Magnite Space.
sections:
A training run connects four decisions: which pretrained behavior you start with, which examples you supply, which parameters can change, and how you judge the result. The buttons in the app correspond to these decisions; a successful job only confirms that the computation completed.

The training base is a compatible Transformers model. A GGUF snapshot belongs to the inference workflow. The dataset supplies the examples, the recipe controls optimization, and the resulting adapter must be evaluated with its matching base.

In Library, download or locate compatible transformer weights. In Training, import a UTF-8 JSONL, CSV or text file. Review the imported row count and inspect the examples before starting.

A useful first dataset is consistent, easy to inspect, and specific to your task. Keep a separate set of evaluation prompts that the model will not train on.

Open the run configuration in Training. Select the base model and imported dataset. Give the adapter a descriptive name. Begin with LoRA and quantization None when your setup supports them.

Choose a batch size and sequence length that fit your machine. The resource estimate is advisory. A successful short run checks the workflow; it does not prove the recipe will generalize.

Keep the comparison simpleRecord the dataset, base snapshot and configuration. Change one important setting at a time.

Follow status, steps and loss in Studio. Open Observatory to review history and compare runs. Enable a validation split when you have enough examples for a held-out set; a split of zero produces no held-out validation measurements.

Missing telemetry means unknown, not zero. Device-wide memory can include other applications. Use the event log to understand a failed or stopped run.

After a successful run, open Adapters and activate the new adapter with its matching base. Try your held-out prompts and compare the responses with the base model. Check the behavior you wanted to improve and a few unrelated prompts.

Export the adapter if you want a portable copy. The export does not include the full base model, which must remain accessible.

articles.title: Settings, storage and privacy
articles.description: Where your data lives, what each Settings page controls, and how to clean up.
sections:
PageControls
GeneralYour name for greetings, keyboard shortcuts, resetting preferences.
AppearanceLight, dark or System theme, interface size and Reduce motion.
ChatSend key, context meter style and automatic compaction.
RuntimeThe default inference engine.
Storage & privacyData directory, model cache, partial downloads, exporting and deleting chats.
NotificationsAlerts when training or downloads finish.
DiagnosticsBackend status, installed engines, hardware and logs.
UpdatesChecking for and installing preview updates.

Conversations, datasets, adapters, Knowledge indexes and Blueprints live in the data directory (~/.magnite on Linux and macOS, %APPDATA%/Magnite on Windows). Downloaded Hub models live in the shared Hugging Face cache, which other tools can also use.

You can choose another data directory; the change applies after a restart and existing data is not moved.

• Partial downloads lists unfinished Hub downloads and their size; delete them to reclaim space.
  • Delete models from Library or a model's Hub page.
  • Export chats saves every conversation to one JSON file; Delete chats… removes them.
Inference, training and document search run locally. Hub search, downloads and update checks use the internet. Diagnostics and logs stay on your computer unless you choose to share them.

articles.title: What does a language model learn?
articles.description: The connection between predictions, loss, gradients and the behavior you observe.
sections:
A causal language model estimates which token could follow the tokens already in context. It produces scores over a vocabulary, which become probabilities. Text generation repeatedly chooses a continuation and extends that context.

That objective is a useful starting point for understanding a training run. The optimization target concerns predictions on examples; the usefulness, accuracy and style of a generated answer are things you still need to evaluate.

Context tokens→Model prediction→Possible next tokens
Loss turns an example into a learning signal

During training, the example supplies target tokens. The loss penalizes predictions that assign insufficient probability to those targets. Many positions in a sequence can contribute to this signal.

Consequently, the examples you choose shape what the optimizer is rewarded for predicting. A repeated phrase, a particular response format, and a domain-specific answer can all become part of the learning signal.
Gradients connect loss to trainable parameters

A gradient describes how a small change to a parameter would change the loss locally. Gradient-based optimization uses this information to adjust trainable parameters over repeated batches. The learning rate influences the scale of the update; actual optimizers may also maintain state from previous updates.

Pretraining and adaptationFine-tuning begins with pretrained parameters. In Magnite Space’s LoRA flow, the base weights stay frozen and the adapter parameters are trained.
A useful way to interpret the result

Consider the objective, the examples and the evaluation together. A lower training loss describes a closer fit to the training objective. To understand the behavior you have actually changed, compare the base and adapted models on requests relevant to your task.

articles.title: Tokens, context and what the model actually sees
articles.description: How text becomes model inputs, and why formatting and length affect your data.
sections: Text is represented through a tokenizer

A tokenizer maps text to entries in a model’s vocabulary. A token may represent a whole word, part of a word, punctuation or another unit. Subword methods make it possible to represent many words using a vocabulary of reusable pieces.

The representation depends on the tokenizer. Equal character counts or word counts do not imply equal token counts, and two models may represent the same string differently.

Original text→Tokenizer + vocabulary→Token IDs
Formatting becomes part of the input

Conversation records contain roles and content. Magnite Space uses the tokenizer’s chat template when available to serialize those messages; otherwise it falls back to readable role/content text. The resulting sequence is what training receives.

The current trainer applies its objective to the full formatted sequence. Message roles alone do not turn on assistant-only loss masking.
Length limits change the examples you train on

Magnite Space’s training sequence-length setting limits the tokenized input. If an example is truncated, some of the original text is excluded. Inspect long examples with particular care when the useful answer is near the end.

A chat context window is a separate runtime limit. Magnite Space’s context calculation also reserves room for the requested output. Changing a training sequence-length setting does not increase that inference limit.
Questions to bring to your dataset

How much of each formatted example fits? Are repeated wrappers consuming space? Does the base model expect a particular chat format? These questions help connect the source data to the actual input representation.

articles.title: Model weights, GGUF and adapters
articles.description: Understand the artifacts you work with and what each one can change.
sections:
ArtifactWhat it is for
Transformers base weightsThe pretrained model used by Magnite Space’s LoRA training flow.
GGUF modelA model for local inference with a compatible llama.cpp engine.
LoRA adapterA small learned addition that needs its matching base weights.
Choose a base for your task

Check the model’s architecture, tokenizer, license and runtime support. Start with a model your machine can load reliably. A larger download is not automatically a better starting point for your data or device.

Use a stable base snapshot when comparing experiments. Keep the same model and evaluation prompts while you test a dataset or recipe change.

Magnite Space separates inference from training. Auto selects a compatible inference engine; individual overrides live in Playground model settings. Training uses the Python training runtime and supported transformer weights.

An installed package does not guarantee that every architecture or device will work. Read the capability message and resource estimate for the configuration you select.

articles.title: What your dataset is teaching
articles.description: Look beyond valid rows: the patterns, omissions and inconsistencies your model will see.
sections:
Choose a task you can recognize in the output. For example: answer support requests in a specific structure, extract a few fields, or follow a concise house style. Write representative examples of the desired response.

Training data should demonstrate the behavior you want. Repeated contradictions make the task harder to learn.
The signal includes more than the answer

A training record can carry several patterns at once: subject matter, response length, tone, formatting, repeated boilerplate and the relationship between the request and its answer. If all examples use the same long introduction, that introduction is part of the signal as well.

Inspect examples together with their source and intended use. An import can be perfectly valid while the examples omit the situations you care about or give inconsistent answers to similar requests.

What to inspectWhat it can reveal
Source and collection contextWhich users, tasks or environments the examples represent.
Repeated answers and templatesWhich patterns dominate the training signal.
Length and formattingWhether important parts may be truncated or special formatting overrepresented.
Conflicting targetsWhether similar inputs ask the model to learn incompatible behavior.

• Remove empty rows, malformed records and accidental duplicates.
  • Keep instructions and answers consistent with the intended task.
  • Inspect unusually long examples; a sequence-length limit can truncate them.
  • Use data you are allowed to process, and remove content that should not become part of an adapter.

A held-out set should represent the same task without duplicating the training examples. Magnite Space can reserve a seeded validation split when enabled. It needs enough rows to keep both training and evaluation nonempty.

Also keep a fixed set of real prompts for manual comparisons. Similar losses do not guarantee equally useful responses.

Current Magnite Space behaviorConversation records use the tokenizer’s chat template when available, with a readable fallback. The trainer learns from the full formatted sequence; importing messages does not enable assistant-only loss masking.

articles.title: Data distributions, duplication and leakage
articles.description: Understand which patterns dominate, which cases are missing, and what a split really separates.
sections:
A collection of examples has a composition: sources, topics, languages, answer lengths and recurring templates. Understanding that composition is part of understanding the experiment.

This example supplies far more refund-related patterns than other situations. A single average evaluation score could conceal weak behavior on the small category. The numbers illustrate composition; they are not measurements of your files.
Repeated records can cross a split

A random row split can put copies or near-copies of an example on both sides. Evaluation then measures familiarity with related material as well as performance on unseen cases. Review duplicates and shared origins before treating a held-out set as independent.
The boundary should match the question

If you want to evaluate new users, documents or conversations, separate those groups across the split. If the intended use concerns future data, consider the time boundary. Row-level randomness alone does not enforce these distinctions.

Magnite Space’s current splitThe validation split is a seeded row-level split. It does not automatically deduplicate, stratify, or isolate users, documents and time periods. Prepare those boundaries in your source datasets when needed.

Leakage occurs when evaluation information influences model development in a way that would not be available for a genuinely new request. Fit learned preprocessing on training data, and use the corresponding transformation on held-out data. Revising a recipe repeatedly against the same test set also changes what that score can tell you.

articles.title: Dataset structure and conversation formats
articles.description: How text, prompt/response pairs and messages are represented and imported.
sections:
Magnite Space accepts UTF-8 JSONL, CSV and plain text. JSONL stores one complete JSON object per line. Message records preserve roles; a prompt/response pair is normalized into a user message and an assistant message.

These are format examplesThe sample contains only two rows. It is meant to test ingestion, not train a useful assistant.

You can also use a text field, instruction/input/output records, or a messages array with valid role and content strings. Plain-text import creates normalized training examples.

Keep a consistent schema within a file. Check row-level errors rather than assuming an import skipped a malformed record.

Open Training, import the file, and verify the row count and dataset selection. Dataset files referenced by queued or running jobs cannot be deleted. Magnite Space’s current CSV field limit is 131,072 characters.

For conversational examples, inspect how the selected model’s tokenizer formats messages. The training sequence length is a separate setting from the number of dataset rows.

articles.title: How training parameters change the experiment
articles.description: Connect learning rate, batch size, sequence length and rank to the learning process.
sections:
ControlWhat to consider
Learning rateThe starting optimizer step size. Record it and compare controlled runs.
Epochs / max stepsHow long training runs. A positive max-step setting limits the run by optimizer steps.
Batch sizeExamples processed together per device. It affects memory requirements.
Sequence lengthThe maximum training input length after tokenization; longer examples can be truncated.
Rank / alphaAdapter size and scaling.
Validation split / seedHeld-out evaluation and reproducibility of the data split.

Save a named configuration, use the same base snapshot and dataset, and change one major control at a time. A seed helps make a comparison more repeatable, but results can still differ across hardware and runtime versions.

Use a short run to check that the chosen inputs and runtime work. Evaluate quality with held-out examples before increasing the duration.

Magnite Space probes supported quantization and estimates memory for the selected recipe. Treat the estimate as advisory. If a target-module name is not present on an architecture, the current fallback may use all-linear; inspect the saved run and log.

articles.title: Generalization and the meaning of evaluation
articles.description: Separate fitting your examples from evidence about behavior on new inputs.
sections: Fitting examples and handling new inputs

Generalization concerns performance beyond the examples used to fit a model. Overfitting describes a model fitting the training data more closely than is useful for unseen data. Different data, model capacity and optimization choices can change this balance.

For a language-model adapter, examine both the recorded objective and the behavior on representative requests. Success on the examples used for training is limited evidence about new inputs.
Training, validation and test sets answer different questions

SetRole in the experiment
TrainingExamples used for parameter updates.
ValidationHeld-out examples used while comparing recipes and making development choices.
TestA separate evaluation reserved for judging the resulting choices.

Check how each set was collected and whether related records overlap. A named split is not, by itself, evidence of independence.
A metric is a view of behavior

Training loss summarizes the fitted objective. Validation loss can help reveal a widening gap between training and held-out behavior. Rising validation loss alongside falling training loss is a reason to investigate overfitting, rather than assume more updates will help.

Compare loss with consistent preprocessing and evaluation data. Also inspect task-specific behavior: answer correctness, useful formatting, failure cases and performance on less common inputs. A single average can leave important differences hidden.

Magnite Space records held-out evaluation loss when a validation split is enabled, at epoch boundaries. A split of zero does not produce that evidence. It does not automatically run a separate final test suite or certify the quality of a completed adapter.

articles.title: Interpreting loss and runtime measurements
articles.description: What the recorded signals mean, which comparisons are meaningful, and where uncertainty remains.
sections: Training loss measures the objective on training examples. A lower value by itself does not establish that the adapter performs better on new requests. Check outputs against your task and compare with the base model.

Enable a validation split before starting if you want held-out validation loss. With the split enabled, Magnite Space records evaluation loss at epoch boundaries. Runs without that measurement should show it as unavailable.

Compare runs using the same data split and prompts. If training loss improves while validation worsens, inspect possible overfitting or a mismatch between training and evaluation data before extending the run.

SignalHow to read it
Loss / validationRecorded measurements for the selected run.
Steps per secondTraining throughput, not generated chat tokens per second.
Device memory / utilizationDevice-wide usage; other processes may contribute.
Missing valueUnknown or not measured, never an assumed zero.

Inspect the event log for failures, preserve the run configuration, and test the adapter on fixed prompts. Use Observatory for comparisons. A cancelled job and a completed job are different outcomes; check the recorded status before using an output.

articles.title: Where training memory goes
articles.description: Weights, activations and optimizer state contribute to the memory a run needs.
sections:
Loading base weights is only part of the budget. Adapter training also needs intermediate activations and optimizer-related state. A model that fits for inference can still exceed memory during training.

Quantized base weights may reduce one part of the requirement. They do not remove all other allocations.
If a run runs out of memory

1. Read the reported error and the capability probe.
  2. Stop other work that uses the same device.
  3. Try a smaller batch or training sequence length.
  4. Use a smaller compatible base model if necessary.
  5. Consider a supported quantized training configuration.

Preserve a copy of the recipe so you can tell which change helped. Avoid treating a resource estimate as a promise that a job will fit.

Supported devices and optional packages vary by build. Magnite Space’s Diagnostics view shows package availability and device measurements. Missing measurements remain unknown. The current app does not support QLoRA on macOS.

articles.title: LoRA, QLoRA and the base model
articles.description: What adapter training changes, what stays frozen, and where memory savings come from.
sections: A small addition to a frozen base

LoRA keeps the pretrained weights fixed and learns smaller update matrices. The trained adapter works together with the base model. You can keep separate adapters for different tasks without copying a full trained model for each one.

Base weights
Frozen
+
LoRA adapter
Trainable
→
Adapted model
Base + adapter

Rank controls the size of the low-rank update. A larger rank adds trainable parameters and memory cost; it is not a guarantee of better output. Alpha affects update scaling, and target modules determine where the adapter is applied.

Quantization stores base weights at lower precision. Training adapters on a quantized base can reduce memory needs, but still requires memory for activations and training state. Supported quantization methods depend on the backend and hardware.

In Magnite SpaceUse the capability probe for the selected environment. QLoRA is not supported on macOS in the current app. A GGUF inference model is not a substitute for the transformer base used by this training flow.

articles.title: Retrieval, context and model knowledge
articles.description: How local documents influence an answer without changing the model weights.
sections: How retrieval works in Magnite Space

Knowledge imports documents, divides their text into chunks and stores searchable embeddings locally. A query retrieves relevant passages that can be added to the chat context. This does not update the chat model’s weights.
Choose the workflow for your goal

For changing reference material, try retrieval and check the passages it finds. For a repeated output behavior, consider an adapter and evaluate it on held-out examples. You can use both workflows, but evaluate each contribution separately.

The first embedding-model use can require a download. Current chunk size and overlap controls are measured in words. Scanned PDFs need OCR that Magnite Space does not currently provide.

A retrieved passage does not guarantee a faithful response from the model. Read the source passage and verify important details. Removing a document from the index does not remove the original source file.

articles.title: Adapters, base compatibility and portability
articles.description: Understand what you are loading, switching and exporting with an adapter.
sections:
Open Adapters after a successful run and activate the new adapter. Magnite Space uses its recorded base model with the PEFT/torch inference flow. Activation restarts the inference model; it is not a zero-restart multi-adapter switch.

Make sure the resolved base snapshot remains accessible. An adapter is not a standalone set of full model weights.

Use the evaluation prompts you set aside before training. Check formatting, correctness and task behavior. Also inspect whether an unrelated prompt has become less useful.

Deactivating the adapter unloads inference. Load the base model again to compare the unadapted behavior.

Magnite Space exports an adapter archive with metadata and safetensors weights. It does not include the base model. Import expects a valid Magnite Space adapter export and rejects a duplicate registered ID.

Keep a known-good export before deleting an adapter. Record the dataset and run configuration alongside your result.

articles.title: Investigating a training problem
articles.description: Interpret errors and unexpected behavior using your inputs, configuration and runtime.
sections: Check the encoding, file format and row number in the error. JSONL needs one valid JSON object per line. Prompt/response values need nonempty strings. The current CSV field-size limit can reject oversized records.
Base model or runtime is unavailable

Confirm that training is using compatible transformer weights, not a GGUF-only snapshot. Review installed package versions in Diagnostics and the selected run’s capability message. Keep the original base snapshot accessible when activating an adapter.
Training stops with a memory error

Inspect the device-wide memory reading and other active work. Reduce batch size or sequence length, then retry a short run with one change recorded. Use a smaller model if the available memory remains insufficient.
Training completes but the output is poor

Inspect your dataset for inconsistent targets and repeated examples. Compare the adapter against the base on prompts that were not used for training. Confirm that the intended adapter is active. A successful training status confirms execution, not model quality.

Record the configuration and error text. Settings → Diagnostics offers a reviewable report with runtime details. Local logs can include file paths and model names; inspect what you copy before sharing.

articles.title: Machine learning vocabulary
articles.description: Definitions of the terms used across model training, data preparation and inference.
sections:
TermMeaning here
Base modelThe pretrained weights an adapter is built for.
AdapterLearned task-specific parameters used with the base.
DatasetThe examples imported for a training job.
TokenA piece of text produced by the model’s tokenizer.
Sequence lengthThe training input-length limit after tokenization.
EpochA pass through the training examples.
StepA recorded optimizer update in the run.
ValidationEvaluation on held-out examples.
QuantizationA lower-precision representation of model weights.
RAGRetrieval-augmented generation: add relevant passages to the context.

A token count is not a word count. Training sequence length and a chat context window are related to input length but belong to different workflows. In Magnite Space’s retrieval controls, chunk size and overlap are currently measured in words.
